caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1401 of 2002.
lawyer:
Abdus Salam Khan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi. Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record------For the Petitioners. 
SS Halder, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr Bivash Chandra, Advocate-on-Record------For Respondent No. 1
Not represented------Respondent Nos. 2-16.

Abul Bashar and others ------ Petitioners
Vs
Prafulla Kumar Das and Others  ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J : This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated June 26, 2002 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4624 of 2000 discharging the Rule obtained against the order dated September 19, 2000 (order No. 16 dated 19-9-2000) of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Charfesson, Bhola, in Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 rejecting the application seeking stay of further proceedings of the said Execution Case. The Execution case was filed pursuant to final decree dated 31-8-1998 passed in a suit for partition Title Suit No. 8 of 1959 (Title Suit No. 28 of 1987). 

 2. The plaintiff-petitioners have filed the Title Suit No. 96 of 1997 seeking declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 28 of 1987 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Bhola is void and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for further declaration that the plaintiffs have title in the property described in the 'ga' schedule attached to the plaint. 

 3. The plaintiff filed application in the Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 seeking stay of further proceeding of the said Execution Case and the same was rejected on August 12, 1999. The plaintiffs also filed an application in the Execution Case with the prayer for recalling the writ of delivery of possession and the Court allowed the same. But subsequently, on the prayer of the decree- holder, the said order was vacated. As against the said order of the Court of Assistant Judge the plaintiffs filed revisional application before the High Court Division and the same was rejected having not been pressed. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed an application in the Execution Case seeking stay of the further proceedings of the said Execution Case. The Court of Assistant Judge rejected the said prayer by the order dated September 19, 2000. The petitioners as against the said order moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division in the background of the facts and circumstances of the case observed since the petitioners were not party in the partition suit application filed seeking stay of the Execution case in the light of the provision of Order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure was a misconceived one. The High Court Division further observed that mere filing of a suit challenging a decree by the 3rd party cannot be a ground for stay of further proceedings of the Execution Case started pursuant to a decree in suit wherein petitioner(s) was not a party and as petitioners suit is not a suit against the decree-holder at the instance of the judgment debtor provision of Order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application. 

 5. The High Court Division maintained the order of the learned Assistant Judge rejecting the petitioners' prayer for stay of the further proceedings of Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 on the view that petitioners were not parties in the Partition Suit No. 28 of 1987, pursuant to a decree wherein the Execution Case has been filed and in that state of the matter the petitioners cannot take recourse to the provision of Order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure in support of their prayer for stay of the further proceedings of the Execution Case. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the petitioners could not take any exception to the said findings and decisions of the High Court Division while discharging the Rule. Since the petitioners were not parties in the Partition Suit No. 28 of 1987 and their suit being not by the judgment debtor against the decree holder of the Court that passed the decree in the partition suit and consequently, as provision of Order XXI rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be availed of by the petitioners the High Court Division as well as the Court of Assistant Judge were quite correct in rejecting the prayer for stay. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that earlier petitioners filed an application for stay and the same was rejected and thereupon they filed an application for recalling the writ of delivery of possession which was allowed by the Court, but later on the Court recalled same on the prayer of the decree holder and as against that the petitioners moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction but as they finally did not press the revisional application the same was rejected as not pressed. Thereafter, they filed the application seeking stay of further proceedings of the Execution Case and same having been rejected moved the High Court Division, but without desired result.
